title: Endless swapchain-recreate loop when the surface reports a zero extent
explanation: AcquireNextImage returns is_outdated. RecreateSwapchain calls Swapchain::Create, which clears is_outdated and then returns early when maxImageExtent is 0 (vk_swapchain.cpp:151), leaving the old, retired swapchain in place. The next AcquireNextImage on it returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR again, so the loop never ends. It runs with swapchain_mutex held, so WaitPresent (and therefore BlitScreen::WaitIdle) blocks too. Composite guards with IsShown() (not minimised), but a frame already queued on the present thread when the window is minimised, or a zero-size surface without minimise, still reaches this loop. A first Create that returns early leaves swapchain null and the next acquire uses a null handle.
suggested_fix: In CopyToSwapchainImpl, bound the loop and drop the frame (DiscardFrame) when Create did not produce a swapchain; have Swapchain::Create report whether it succeeded and keep is_outdated set on early return.
how_to_verify: Minimise the window (or resize it to 0 height) while async_presentation is on and frames are queued; check whether the VulkanPresent thread spins in CopyToSwapchainImpl. Or add a log line in the loop and count iterations.

title: Anti-aliasing pass destroyed while earlier frames may still be using it
explanation: RefreshResources destroys the FXAA/SMAA object (images, views, pipelines, descriptor sets) before ReleaseRawImages() waits on resource_ticks, so GPU work submitted for earlier frames can still reference them. SetAntiAliasPass (lines 243-249) replaces the pass on a setting change with no wait at all. The destructors are defaulted, so vkDestroy* and allocation release happen immediately. Trigger: guest framebuffer size or pixel format change, or switching the AA setting at runtime with FXAA/SMAA active.
suggested_fix: Wait on all resource_ticks (as SetPostProcessPass does) before any emplace on anti_alias, or move the wait loop into a helper called from both places.
how_to_verify: Run with the Vulkan validation layer, enable FXAA, change the AA setting or trigger a guest resolution change, and look for VUID errors about destroying objects in use.

title: Every pooled frame triggers a full present-pipeline rebuild after a resize or startup
explanation: The size test is made against the individual pooled frame. Up to seven frames still have the old size, so each of them sets resource_update_required, which runs WaitIdle (WaitPresent + scheduler.Finish + vkDeviceWaitIdle), SetWindowAdaptPass (layers.clear(), new window-adapt pass, and all layers rebuilt with FSR/AA/post images and pipelines on the next draw) and resets image_index. A window resize or first start therefore costs up to image_count full stalls and rebuilds instead of one.
suggested_fix: Track the layout size the pass was built for; rebuild the pass and layers once when it changes, and only call RecreateFrame (after the wait) for a frame whose size differs.
how_to_verify: Drag-resize the window or start a game and count SetWindowAdaptPass calls (log or breakpoint) per resize; expect more than one.

title: FxChain snapshot copies all entries every frame just to read the generation counter
explanation: Layer::SetPostProcessPass runs on the render thread for every non-applet layer on every composited frame (HAS_RESHADE). Snapshot() takes the FxChain mutex and deep-copies the vector of FxChainEntry (two strings plus a std::map of arrays each), so a chain with several effects costs dozens of heap allocations per frame to read one atomic. PostProcessChain::UpdateUniforms then copies the per-entry value map again (EntryValues) every frame.
suggested_fix: Add FxChain::Generation() returning the atomic, and use it here. Have the chain read overrides under the lock without copying, or cache them until a value-change counter moves.
how_to_verify: Profile allocations per frame with a 4-5 effect chain enabled (heap profiler or counting operator new in a debug build); compare with the chain disabled.

title: Per-frame std::vector allocations on the composite path
explanation: WindowAdaptPass::Draw allocates three vectors every composited frame and the [=] lambda handed to scheduler.Record copies them again. PostProcessChain::UpdateUniforms (post_process.cpp:692) allocates a staging vector per effect per frame, and UpdateDescriptors allocates image-info vectors per pass. With frame generation these frames can be produced above 100 per second, so the allocator is hit several times per frame on the render thread.
suggested_fix: Use small fixed-size arrays (layers are few) or reusable member buffers, and move rather than copy into the recorded lambda.
how_to_verify: Count allocations per Composite call with a debug allocator hook, with one layer and with post-processing enabled.

title: Post-process chain reset for an applet frame is not waited on and leaves the cache keys stale
explanation: When a layer sees a framebuffer without the Recording layer-stack bit, the chain is destroyed with no wait on resource_ticks and post_process_generation, post_process_enabled and post_process_extent are left unchanged. If the same Layer object later gets a normal frame, the early-return test at lines 268-272 matches the old keys and the chain is never rebuilt, so effects stay off until the chain generation, enabled flag or extent changes. It only matters if one Layer alternates between the two kinds of frame; I did not confirm that happens.
suggested_fix: Wait on resource_ticks before the reset and reset post_process_generation to a sentinel (for example 0) so the next non-applet frame rebuilds.
how_to_verify: Find a game where the same layer index carries both recording and non-recording frames (for example an applet overlay), enable a post chain, and check whether effects disappear after the applet frame.

title: vkDeviceWaitIdle in BlitScreen::WaitIdle runs without the queue submit mutex
explanation: vkDeviceWaitIdle needs external synchronisation with every queue. WaitPresent is called first and scheduler.Finish second, so a Present lambda still sitting in an undispatched scheduler chunk can enqueue a frame after WaitPresent returned. The present thread then submits and presents while this thread is in vkDeviceWaitIdle, without scheduler.submit_mutex. Swapchain::Create takes that mutex around its WaitIdle; this site and the RendererVulkan destructor do not. The window is narrow because Composite ends with DispatchWork.
suggested_fix: Call scheduler.Finish() first, then WaitPresent(), then take scheduler.submit_mutex around vkDeviceWaitIdle.
how_to_verify: Run with synchronization validation while changing the scaling filter during gameplay with async_presentation on; look for host-synchronisation errors on the queue.

title: Present manager teardown does not wait for the last submitted copy and may race the present thread
explanation: RendererVulkan's destructor body calls vkDeviceWaitIdle, but the present thread is only joined later, when present_manager's members are destroyed. A frame still in present_queue at that moment is submitted after the wait, and frames, semaphores and the command pool are then destroyed without a second wait. Worker lambdas that capture PresentManager::this are also destroyed after it (Scheduler is declared before present_manager, so its worker joins later). Normal shutdown probably drains the queue first; I did not confirm that.
suggested_fix: Request stop and join the present thread explicitly in the destructor, then WaitIdle under submit_mutex before the frames are destroyed; finish the scheduler before present_manager is destroyed.
how_to_verify: Close the emulator while frame generation is running at a high frame rate, with validation layers on, and look for errors about destroying a semaphore, fence or command buffer in use.

title: Exceptions other than surface-lost on the present thread terminate the process
explanation: CopyToSwapchain rethrows any vk::Exception that is not VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR (for example a failed submit or VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST). On the VulkanPresent thread nothing catches it, so std::terminate runs. In sync mode the same exception propagates through Composite instead. Swapchain::Present only logs other present errors, so device loss reported by present is not surfaced on either path.
suggested_fix: Catch vk::Exception in PresentThread, call device.ReportLoss() for VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, and stop the thread or discard frames cleanly.
how_to_verify: Force a device loss (driver reset or TDR) with async_presentation on and see whether the process aborts from the present thread instead of reporting the loss.

title: applet_frame is default-initialised, so its width and height are read uninitialised
explanation: Frame::width, height and index have no initialiser. RenderAppletCaptureLayer creates the image at CaptureFormat, then BlitScreen::DrawToFrame compares layout.width/height with the indeterminate frame->width/height (undefined behaviour). If they differ, which is almost certain, it runs WaitIdle and RecreateFrame, which replaces the freshly created capture image, view and framebuffer with a swapchain-format image. This happens once, at the first capture.
suggested_fix: Initialise width, height and index in Frame, or set applet_frame.width/height from VideoCore::Capture::Layout when the image is created.
how_to_verify: Build with MSan or an /RTC-style check, or set a breakpoint in DrawToFrame on the first applet capture and inspect frame->width.

title: Cached LSFG shader size comes straight from the cache file
explanation: word_count is read from the cache file and used for an allocation before any size check. The header hash covers the source DLL, not the cache body, so a corrupted file with a large count raises std::bad_alloc (or a huge allocation) instead of returning false and rebuilding the cache. A truncated file is fine; the later Read fails.
suggested_fix: Reject word_count above the remaining file size divided by four (or a fixed maximum) before allocating.
how_to_verify: Patch four bytes of the first module's word_count in the cache file to 0x7FFFFFFF and start with frame generation enabled.

title: Generation descriptors are cached on the raw VkImageView handle and rewritten while possibly in use
explanation: SetTarget skips the descriptor write when the handle value is unchanged. If a frame's storage view is destroyed and recreated (RecreateFrame) and the driver returns the same handle value, the descriptor keeps pointing at the destroyed view. When the handle does change, UpdateDescriptorSets rewrites sets that earlier submitted dispatches may still be using, with no wait.
suggested_fix: Key the cache on a frame generation counter incremented in RecreateFrame, and wait for the slot's last tick before rewriting its sets.
how_to_verify: Toggle frame generation or resize the window repeatedly with validation layers on and look for descriptor-in-use or invalid-view errors.
